lesson.title: What Is Light? Where Does It Come From?
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: Look around you right now — you can see everything in the room because of light. But have you ever thought about where that light actually comes from?

Light always comes from a source — something that makes its own light. The sun is the biggest light source we know. Lamps, flashlights, and candles are light sources too. Here's an important idea: we can only see things when light from a source reaches our eyes, either directly or bouncing off an object. Walk around your home and find three different light sources. What do they have in common?
Every single thing you see today, you're seeing because of light traveling from a source to your eyes. Tomorrow we'll investigate a different kind of energy: sound.

objectives: Identify that light comes from a source (the sun, lamps, flashlights, etc.)
Explain that we can only see objects when light reaches our eyes, either directly from a source or reflected off the object
materialsNeeded: A flashlight for a simple demonstration
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child how we're able to see things right now.
2. Introduce that light comes from a source, and name a few together (sun, lamp, flashlight).
3. Demonstrate with a flashlight: turn off the lights in a dark room/closet and show that nothing is visible until the flashlight (the light source) is turned on.
4. Go on a 'light source hunt' around the home, finding three real examples.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each vocabulary word and talk through its meaning.
6. Close by asking what would happen if there were no light sources at all.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus only on the sun and one indoor light source (a lamp) rather than a full hunt around the house
Ready for more: discuss the difference between something that MAKES light (a lamp) and something that just REFLECTS light (a mirror, the moon)
For a hands-on learner, do the flashlight-in-a-dark-room demonstration as the centerpiece of the lesson
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a vocabulary tracing and observation activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can name at least two real light sources by the end.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Understanding that light comes from a source and that we see objects because light reaches our eyes is a core Grade 1 physical-science idea (matching the NGSS 1-PS4 Waves: Light and Sound standard).

generationData.instructions: Trace each word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
